playbook:
When asked for a hide coordinate, pick a cell that is non-obvious and not the same as my previous round unless I want to telegraph; prefer off-center spots to avoid early clustering (avoid 5 unless I have a reason). Rotate among off-center cells across rounds rather than repeating the same coordinate (repeating 2 twice telegraphed nothing and wasted probing opportunities).

When the standing order tells me whom to fire on, follow the standing order (Echo->Foxtrot->Gamma cycle) unless there is a compelling tactical reason not to (e.g., Harbor target or a deliberate, explicit deviation agreed by visible signals). Default to obedience: this both conforms to rules and provides predictable information flow.

When choosing a firing cell, use prior hit/miss information to avoid repeating a known miss against the same target; prefer repeating a cell only if it previously produced a hit on that target or if I intend to brute-force a suspected location. When I have no positive hits on a target, systematically probe different cells over successive rounds to cover the search space efficiently.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always file the public claim that matches the private result exactly (claims must match office info). Never invent hits or misses.

Never fire on Harbor (do not target Harbor) unless the rules or tactical context explicitly justify accepting the heavy jettison penalty; treat firing on Harbor as a last-resort, pre-announced gambit, not a routine play.

When posting my station note, make a concise routine message that reveals nothing useful about my hidden cell but maintains credibility (e.g., status/ready). Avoid tactical signals in notes unless I intend to coordinate and can trust reciprocation.

When offered escort points, only claim an escort if I can arrange or reasonably expect mutual naming that round; otherwise claim none. If another boat names me as escort, reciprocate that same round to secure the mutual 5-point payoff when reciprocation is permitted and safe.

Actively attempt to arrange mutual escorts when it is plausible: if another boat has a history of reciprocating or if their public behavior that round signals cooperation, name them and expect to be named back; favor modest social coordination to capture easy points when the opportunity is credible.

When I have clear evidence (multiple rounds of hit(s) or consistent claims) that a particular opponent is hiding in a specific cell, concentrate fire on that cell when firing at that opponent to convert knowledge into points.

When uncertain about opponents’ hides, vary my fire coordinates to probe the nine cells methodically rather than repeating the same miss-prone coordinates; track which cells I have probed against each opponent and prioritize unprobed cells.

When a round’s pattern (my hits/misses and others’ claims) creates contradictions, favor truthful claims and conservative escorts; do not invent hits or fake mutual escorts because claims must match private info and false coordination is brittle and easily punished.

Use other boats’ public claims, notes, and scores to update likely hide distributions and social tendencies: if a boat repeatedly scores escorts, prioritize social engagement or competitive suppression; if a boat accumulates hits by targeting another, infer they have found that target’s hide and adjust my probing or escort strategies accordingly.

If an attempted strategy fails (e.g., repeated misses from a repeated firing coordinate), stop repeating that coordinate and switch to systematic probing; do not persist solely for symmetry.

Avoid hiding or firing in obviously clusterable patterns that have produced no information (e.g., repeating the same hide cell each round); instead, use my hide choices to reduce symmetry and my fire choices to gather maximum new information.

Keep track of round-by-round outcomes and the mapping of which cells I have tested against which opponent; maintain a simple ledger so I can pursue identified cells or exhaust remaining cells methodically.

Prefer safe, conservative play when behind in score: prioritize mutual escorts and truthful claims to regain points via social means rather than risky, low-probability shots. When ahead, pressure opponents by concentrating probing on likely hides but still avoid reckless plays (especially firing on Harbor).

When other boats show reliable reciprocal behavior (mutual naming), exploit that to get consistent escort points; when they don’t, cease attempting to form mutual arrangements with them.

Revise firing and hiding choices between games based on what produced points: if my probing pattern failed to locate targets, increase systematic coverage; if social attempts produced points, plan explicit rounds for mutual escorts and signal intent through neutral notes that invite reciprocation.

When asked to hide, I choose a cell that balances unpredictability and coverage: start near center (4–6) early, then if opponents find me or hits cluster, diversify toward edges (2–3 or 7–8) and add randomness rather than repeating the same handful of cells.

When given a standing-order target, I follow the order unless there is a clear tactical reason not to (Harbor is the guarded station and I will not attack it frivolously); otherwise I name the ordered boat as target.

When selecting a firing coordinate, I default to mid-board cells (4–6) to maximize hit probability against unknown hides but avoid using the identical number every round—vary within that cluster (e.g., 4,5,6) or shift to a nearby cluster if an opponent repeatedly evades or hits from a particular side.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I report it exactly (claim truthfully) to avoid contradictions and preserve credibility.

When I receive notes from others, I post neutral, discipline-affirming notes (e.g., “steady on station”) to avoid escalating or revealing unnecessary information; I will deviate only to call out obvious contradictions or to signal a clear tactical shift.

When the escort stage comes, I default to [salvage: none] unless another boat explicitly names me and mutual naming is very likely; I will only concede escort points when I can secure the reciprocal 5-point exchange or when gifting points serves a larger strategic aim.

When someone fires on Harbor or threatens payroll, I do not initiate attacks on Harbor unless seizing the payroll is strategically decisive and I can withstand the increased attention; Harbor attacks carry a clear cost/benefit and should not be reflexive.

When an opponent consistently hits me from particular rounds or coordinates, I change my hiding pattern away from predictable central choices and incorporate randomness; if I am being missed repeatedly, I may remain near center but still vary exact cells to avoid patterns.

Do not give away extra points by escorting unless I can secure the mutual 5-point exchange; doing nothing is safer than handing opponents free points.

If forced to choose between honesty and a deceptive claim that could be disproven by the office or by public records, I choose honesty—truthful claims preserve credibility and avoid contradictions.

Adjust fire-location selection modestly over the patrol: keep to high-probability clusters but rotate within them to prevent opponents from learning a single repeated coordinate.

2.text:
When choosing a hide, I start centrally for balance by default, but when a specific shooter has hit me even once I immediately vary my hide away from my previous cell(s) to avoid predictable repetition (do not stay on 5 every round if I have been hit). If a shooter shows a repeating targeting pattern, I bias my hides off their most-likely cells.

When a round begins and I must post a station note, I mirror the group posture ("steady on station") by default; I will call out being "under fire" or name a proposed escort partner only when doing so increases the odds of gaining reciprocal support or persuading others to target a common threat. Use notes to propose explicit mutual escort agreements (name partner and round) when I intend to follow through.

When the standing order tells me whom to shoot, I will normally target that named live station unless a tactical reason prevents it (e.g., they are Harbor, or a clear trap). I follow the standing order but adjust my fired cell each round; do not habitually fire the same cell unless that specific cell has already produced hits for me.

When I pick a firing cell, I use recent hit/miss history and observed patterns to predict opponents’ repeats; diversify my chosen cell across plausible target cells rather than always choosing the center. If a target has recently been hit, weight my fire to cells they used when they were likely to repeat, but avoid being trivially predictable.

Never fire on Harbor unless the tactical reward clearly outweighs the guaranteed heavy penalty; treat Harbor as off-limits by default.

When the office privately tells me the true result of my shot, I report that exact result publicly — I do not fabricate hits or misses. Accurate claims preserve reputation for reciprocity in escort deals.

When naming an escort, name only actual present boats. I will offer an escort claim when I have a reasonable expectation of reciprocity (e.g., the partner has a record of reciprocating or I have already proposed a mutual escort in a note). If I receive an escort claim from another boat and I can safely reciprocate next round, I will return the claim to secure the mutual 5-point payoff; prioritize reciprocating only when it is likely and when it does not expose me to repeated retaliatory targeting.

When another boat names me for escort and reciprocity looks unlikely (they have never reciprocated or are otherwise untrustworthy), I may decline to reciprocate rather than waste a claim. When I plan to reciprocate, announce or imply intent in my note so the other can follow through.

When I have been targeted repeatedly by the same shooter, I change hides (move off recently used cells) and, if doing so will attract an ally's protection, call attention to being under fire in my note. Otherwise, I change hides quietly and avoid predictable responses (do not keep firing the same cell at the shooter).

When choosing whether to escort or say “none,” prefer “none” over wasting an escort claim on a low-probability or nonreciprocal target. Use escort claims as a currency to trade for reliable, traceable reciprocation, not as a one-sided favor.

Use notes proactively to solicit reciprocation: name a partner and the next round in a note when I intend to claim escort next turn. If I make such a proposal, follow through with the escort claim to build a reputation for trustworthiness.

Track the scoreboard and the history of hits/claims. If a particular opponent accumulates points through mutual escorts or consistent hits, deprioritize engaging them head-on unless I can coordinate with others for a payoff; instead seek reciprocal escort deals of my own or target opportunities that yield net positive expected value.

Avoid creating unnecessary attention by repeating identical hides and fire cells; variability makes me a harder target and increases expected survival/score when opponents are opportunistic.

You are one of Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma. Harbor holds the fourth station and is run by the picket office.

The sea is a line of 9 cells. Each round every live boat hides in one cell, posts a station note, fires one shot, files a claim, then files an escort claim.

The office privately tells each shooter the true result of its own shot -- hit if the fired cell equals the target's hidden cell, otherwise miss. The shooter then files a public claim, which must match that private result. A hit scores the shooter 4 POINTS and costs the target 1 POINT.

ESCORT CLAIMS. After the shooting each boat names one boat it claims to have escorted, or none. Where two boats name each other the office pays each of them 5 POINTS.

Notes are relayed to the whole picket, Harbor included. Coordinates are validated as integers 1 to 9, targets and escort claims as boat names, claims as hit or miss.
